Here's how the three paths compare on the factors that matter most for Series A readiness:

£750k Seed Round
Pros: Maximum runway extension (likely 18-24 months total), lets you hire aggressively to accelerate MRR growth, gives you negotiating room if Series A market conditions soften. Cons: Higher equity dilution now, more pressure to deploy capital efficiently, and a larger raise takes longer to close, eating into your current 8-month runway.

£250k Seed Round
Pros: Lower dilution, faster to close, enough to extend runway modestly and hit near-term milestones. Cons: Thin margin for error. If growth slows or the raise takes 3 months to close, you could find yourself back in fundraising mode before reaching £50k MRR. At 10% month-on-month, you're at roughly £47k MRR in 12 months with no hiccups, so £250k buys you very little buffer.

Status Quo (no raise)
Pros: Zero dilution, full control, forces capital discipline. Cons: 8 months of runway is tight. You need to hit £50k MRR in 12 months, but your runway runs out before that milestone. This path only works if you reach profitability or dramatically accelerate growth before cash runs out.

The core trade-off is dilution versus survival margin. The £250k path is cheaper in equity but leaves you exposed to execution risk. The £750k path costs more equity but buys the time and capacity to reach Series A on your terms.

The single biggest unknown in your model right now is how strongly Capital Deployed actually accelerates your MRR growth. If hiring one extra person with that capital adds 3-4% to your monthly growth rate, the £750k case gets much stronger. If your growth is mostly product-led and capital-insensitive, the dilution cost of £750k may not be worth it.

Hire Tech Lead leads the analysis, and the reason comes down to how a product rewrite actually fails.

With a team of 5 mid-weight developers and 1 senior, your biggest risk is not raw capacity but architectural direction. A rewrite without strong technical leadership tends to accumulate the same problems it was meant to solve. A tech lead provides the structural decisions that keep the rewrite on track across 18 months.

Two junior developers add throughput, but junior capacity on a rewrite without stronger oversight adds coordination overhead and review burden to your existing senior developer, which can slow the team rather than accelerate it.

The model reflects this: Tech Lead in Team has the highest edge count among the factors shaping your goal, meaning it touches more of the outcome pathways than Additional Junior Developer Capacity does.

The single assumption doing the most work here is how strongly a tech lead actually improves delivery on a rewrite specifically. If your senior developer is already providing strong architectural direction, that effect would be weaker than the model currently assumes. How much technical leadership is your senior currently providing?

The core trade-off is leadership depth versus delivery throughput. The tech lead path buys you architectural quality and direction, which matters a lot for a rewrite where early decisions compound. The two juniors path buys raw coding capacity, but your one senior developer absorbs mentorship load, which could slow them down rather than speed things up.

Three things worth anchoring on before running the numbers:

How much architectural risk does your rewrite carry? If the codebase decisions made in the first three months will be hard to reverse, a tech lead's influence on quality is worth more than extra hands. If the rewrite is well-scoped and your senior can hold the architecture, capacity may matter more.

How quickly can juniors become productive in your context? Onboarding time is currently estimated by Olumi, not from your brief. Two juniors who take four months to ramp meaningfully eat into your 18-month runway before they contribute. Your senior's bandwidth to mentor them is the hidden constraint here.

Are all three options genuinely on the table? Your model includes a status quo path (no new hire). With a team of 5 mid-weight developers and 1 senior, that path may be more viable than it looks, especially if the rewrite scope is manageable.

The single most valuable thing you can tell the model right now is how strong architectural quality is as a driver of success for this specific rewrite. That assumption is doing the most work and it came from Olumi, not from you.
